intro.author: Paul, according to the letter (1:1). Traditionally accepted as Paul's; many modern scholars think 1 and 2 Timothy and Titus were written by a later follower in his name, while others defend Paul's authorship.
intro.written: If by Paul, probably about AD 62–64, after his first Roman imprisonment, a period Acts does not cover
intro.audience: Timothy, Paul's trusted coworker, whom Paul had left in Ephesus to lead the church there (1:3)
intro.setting: Timothy, from Lystra in Asia Minor, was the son of a Jewish believing mother and a Greek father (Acts 16:1), and had traveled with Paul for years. In Ephesus, teachers were promoting 'fables and endless genealogies' (1:4), forbidding marriage and certain foods (4:3), and treating religion as a way to make money (6:5). The church needed trustworthy leaders and clear order.
intro.purpose: Paul writes so that Timothy will know 'how thou oughtest to behave thyself in the house of God' (3:15): how to oppose false teaching, order worship, choose leaders and care for every group in the church.
intro.bigIdea: Sound teaching and godly leaders keep the church, 'the pillar and ground of the truth', healthy.

outline.title: Caring for the church; godliness and money

commentary.t: THE PASTORAL EPISTLES OF PAUL THE APOSTLE TO TIMOTHY AND TITUS
